properties.chose: The middle path: import_graph keeps whole-node semantics by default (an export→import round trip still reproduces the design, and a document can still remove a property), and merges a partial node's properties into the existing node only when the call asks for it with "merge". Raised by hxm_program's hub feedback 2026-10-20 (item 5: a 454-node partial import silently dropped checksum, checksum_basis and status). Anthony's word 2026-10-21: "Go with (b) Only when asked, with \"merge\" in the call". Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.decision: BL-139's open half, and it is ANTHONY'S because it changes published behaviour rather than fixing a defect. `create_node` merges — its own description says "a partial props object edits" — and `import_graph` does not: re-importing an existing Requirement carrying only `{lineage: "derived"}` fails with `Requirement.statement: required property is missing`. The adopt workflow is import → detect → correct → re-import, so the mismatch lands precisely on the corrective step the skill prescribes. TWO OPTIONS, and the row already judged them: "(2) is honest and cheap; (1) is what the workflow actually wants." (1) MERGE AT PROPERTY LEVEL, like `create_node`. (2) SAY PLAINLY that documents must carry complete nodes — DONE 2026-08-02, in `import_graph`'s own description, so the cheap half is delivered whichever way this goes. THE COST OF (1), which is why it is not a one-word swap and why nobody should make it casually. FIRST, it crosses THREE PUBLISHED BOUNDARIES — `ifc:core-api`, `ifc:graph-export` and `ifc:mcp-tools` — measured, not guessed: `propagate_from("art:export")` reported 705 impacted nodes and `propagate_change` on this session's own edit reported 723, both crossing exactly those three. SECOND, and this is the part no boundary count shows: MERGING MAKES IMPORT NON-IDEMPOTENT FOR DELETION. Today a document is a complete statement of the nodes it names, so re-importing without a property REMOVES it and an export→import round trip reproduces the design exactly. Under (1) a property can only ever be added or changed, never dropped, and restoring a backup would silently retain whatever the live graph had accumulated since. That is a change to what an import MEANS, and it makes the migration and backup jobs this module exists for weaker in exchange for making the adopt loop smoother. THIRD, a middle path exists and should be considered rather than skipped: keep whole-node semantics as the default and let the DOCUMENT ask for merge explicitly (a per-node or per-document flag), so the adopt loop gets what it wants without redefining backup restore for everyone.
properties.name: An import replaces whole nodes unless the call asks it to merge
properties.rationale: Recorded proposed rather than decided, because AGENTS.md puts a Decision reaching `accepted` on the per-session side — that write is the user's signature. Raised now with the measurement attached because the row's framing ("make import_graph merge like create_node") reads as a small fix and the design says otherwise: this is the third time on this project that grep suggested a one-word swap and the graph reported a published-boundary change, and every previous time measuring first was what corrected it.
